why.say:
• A lien: a bill with a legal right to be paid from the settlement before the client's share
• John Doe's $40,000: two liens asserted, five checked and found absent, each recorded with its source
• The money isn't John's until every claim is found, sorted and resolved in writing
• Liens bend differently: statutory to a formula, a Health Plan to a doctrine, a provider balance to negotiation
• Sort one wrong and you overpay John's money away or freeze the payout

theory.say:
• A lien's legal basis decides how far it bends; picture a ladder
• Top: providers on an LOP, a Letter of Protection promising payment from the settlement; very negotiable
• Next: health insurance subrogation, a private plan wanting back what it paid; shaped by made whole and common fund
• Made whole: repaid only once the client is fully compensated; common fund: lienholder shares the cost of recovery
• Lower: Medicare and Medicaid, strict formulas; bottom: ERISA self-funded employer plans, hardest to reduce

frame.say:
• Providers on an LOP sit high: they often reduce to get paid now
• Private health insurance sits moderate, subject to made whole or common fund
• Medicare and Medicaid sit low; ERISA self-funded plans very low, under federal law
• Riverton Spine & Rehab is the LOP provider, top of the ladder; Peach State is fully insured, not ERISA
• Fully insured: the employer bought a policy, so state law generally governs reduction; Atty. Thorne confirms

rules.say:
• Statutory liens (Medicare, Medicaid, hospital, workers' comp) come from law and bend least; contractual claims rest on an agreement
• Inventory every claimant, absent ones too: record where you checked and when, not just “none”
• Two asserted: Peach State and Riverton Spine & Rehab; Harbor Point PIP has no reimbursement right; Crescent can't balance-bill
• Peach State: Atty. Thorne asked for the one-third common-fund share; $1,860.00 minus $620.00 is $1,240.00
• Name doctrines, never choose them; never compromise a lien without his authority or call one invalid to John
